text:
Mike: Heads-up — saw a customer report where a streaming response got truncated client-side, they retried, and ended up with doubled token charges. Suspect interplay between stream-chunk accounting + tool_call attribution when retries increment attempt id.

Sarah: Oof. Do we have a concrete repro? log snippets? :grimacing:

Mike: Pasted a simplified trace from their logs (redacted):
```
2026-10-12T21:04:12Z INFO stream_chunk request_id=rq_91a attempt=0 tokens=120
2026-10-12T21:04:13Z ERROR client_conn_reset request_id=rq_91a
2026-10-12T21:04:14Z INFO tool_call request_id=rq_91a attempt=1 tokens=340
```
They retried with same request_id but attempt=1. Billing pipeline saw both stream_chunk + tool_call and couldn't dedupe because attempt changed.

jun: So the core problem is we currently dedupe by (request_id, route) only when attempt==0? Or we just don't dedupe across attempts at all?

liz: Billing pipeline currently keys on request_id + event_type + event_seq. Retries look like new events because attempt bumps. We do have session_id in some clients but not enforced.

Sarah: Two concerns: correctness (no double-bill) and telemetry/SLAs (we want per-attempt latency and real tokens). I'd vote for requiring stable id (session_id) for the lifetime of retries OR treating stream_chunk events as preliminary and only commit them once finalization event arrives. But the latter hurts live granularity.

mike: Proposal: add these rules:
1) All inbound requests must include session_id header (generated by caller). If missing, we synth one server-side but mark as ephemeral.
2) Each token event includes (request_id, session_id, attempt). Billing dedupe algorithm: prefer highest-attempt finalization marker; but if earlier attempt produced stream tokens that led to server-side tool_calls that are repeated by retry, we dedupe by (session_id, tool_call_id) first.

jun: Example event model I'd expose to billing/telemetry: 
```
{ type: "stream_chunk", session_id: "s_42", request_id: "rq_91a", attempt: 0, tokens: 120 }
{ type: "tool_call", session_id: "s_42", tool_call_id: "tc_7", request_id: "rq_91a", attempt: 1, tokens: 340 }
{ type: "finalize", session_id: "s_42", request_id: "rq_91a", attempt: 1 }
```
Dedupe rule: if same tool_call_id appears multiple times under same session -> keep single. If stream_chunks exist for attempt<finalize.attempt, only include stream tokens up to the earliest tool_call that the server actually executed (so we don't double-count chunks that were retransmitted).

liz: Implementation caveats: we need to surface tool_call_id in user-visible logs & console, and update ingestion to keep small per-session state. That increases memory for high QPS clients but we can TTL by session and size-limit tool_call history. Also need to backfill: historical disputes where customers were charged erroneously.

Sarah: For the console, add an extra column in the per-route token table: "session_id" and a toggle to group by session. Also surface "dedupe_reason" in token timeline so support can explain.

mike: Rollout plan: infer session_id when missing + log noise metric; next release require session_id for newer SDKs. Update billing pipeline to prefer session dedupe and add a fallback TTL-based dedupe for ephemeral sessions.

jun: Telemetry: add metric "billing.dedupe.rate" and a histogram of tokens_per_session to detect regressions. We'll also add an alert if dedupe rate spikes (could indicate a bug).

liz: Does this handle truncation + client double-retry where client generates new request_id? If session_id is stable yes. If client restarts and loses session we fallback to best-effort TTL dedupe which may not catch it. We should update SDKs to persist session_id across retries.

mike: Action items:
- liz: PR to billing ingestion with session_id + tool_call_id fields and TTL cache (2d) (ETA EOD Thu)
- jun: update SDKs to persist session_id and add sample header docs (ETA Mon)
- sarah: console changes spec + mockups for dedupe_reason (ETA next Wed)
- mike: add telemetry metrics and pager rule draft (ETA Fri)

liz: acked. I'll include a small migration doc for support refunds path.

Sarah: Sounds good. If no objections I'll merge this plan. :thumbsup:

mike: +1
